# Real run, 25 Nov 2026 ~14:30-15:05 IST, macOS 26.6.2 (Apple M4 Max, 128 GB), Episode 1 v2 "Your first AI chatbot".
# Java: Eclipse Temurin 21.0.13.1+2 (the JDK a viewer installs in step 1; JAVA_HOME set to it for every run).
# Project generated by start.spring.io on 25 Nov 2026 (web UI, GENERATE button): Spring Boot 4.2.0,
#   Spring AI 2.1.0-M1 (the version start.spring.io writes into pom.xml today), Maven wrapper -> Maven 3.10.1.
#   Also checked with Spring AI 2.1.0 GA (./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-ai.version=2.1.0): same results, see the end.
# Ollama 0.32.13, model qwen3.5:4b (3.3 GB) with think=false, num-ctx=8192, temperature 0.7.
# Node.js v26.13.0, npm 11.20.0, create-vite 9.3.4 -> Vite 8.3.8, React 19.3.1 (official npm registry).
# Ports: Spring app 8080, Vite dev server 5173 (both free, defaults used). Times are wall-clock per HTTP request.
# Two modes: "normal" (Ollama may use the GPU) and "CPU only" (--spring.ai.ollama.chat.num-gpu=0; ollama ps: 100% CPU).
# `ollama stop qwen3.5:4b` before each mode, so the first request of each mode includes loading the model.

$ java -version
openjdk version "21.0.13.1" 2026-11-17 LTS
$ ollama pull qwen3.5:4b
$ cd spring-ai-chat
$ ./mvnw spring-boot:run
Started SpringAiChatApplication in 0.843 seconds (process running for 0.987)
(On a Mac the log also shows one red "ERROR ... Unable to load io.netty.resolver.dns.macos.MacOSDnsServerAddressStreamProvider"
 line on the first AI call. It is harmless: everything works. See NOTES.md.)

It simplifies complex AI workflows by offering ready-to-use components for chatbots, text generation, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), and agent orchestration directly within the Spring framework.

It provides high-level abstractions for common tasks like prompting, tool usage, and agent orchestration while leveraging the familiar Spring ecosystem for configuration and testing.

Spring AI is an open-source project that enables developers to integrate Large Language Models (LLMs) and other generative AI services into existing Java applications using the familiar Spring ecosystem. It simplifies complex tasks like prompt management, context handling, and model orchestration by providing high-level abstractions built on top of libraries such as LangChain4j and Micronaut AI.
   [!] MODEL MISTAKE: Spring AI is NOT built on LangChain4j or "Micronaut AI". Small models make mistakes like this: always check facts.
   (HTTP 200, 4.2 s)

Spring AI is a unified developer experience that bridges the gap between the Spring ecosystem and modern generative AI technologies, allowing developers to easily integrate LLMs and other AI capabilities into their existing Java applications. By providing standard abstractions for prompting, managing context, and handling responses, it simplifies complex AI interactions while maintaining full compatibility with Spring Boot's dependency management and configuration patterns.

## Step 13 check: the page WITHOUT @CrossOrigin (same app, the one line removed)
The page shows: "Sorry, I can't reach the chatbot app. Is it running on http://localhost:8080?"
Browser console (F12): Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:8080/stream?q=...' from origin 'http://localhost:5173' has been
blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.
With @CrossOrigin(origins = "http://localhost:5173") added: answers stream in (above).

## The sneaky setting: think=true (CPU only, model already loaded, final code)
$ ./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.arguments="--spring.ai.ollama.chat.num-gpu=0 --spring.ai.ollama.chat.think=true"
$ curl "localhost:8080/chat?q=What%20is%20Spring%20AI%3F%20Answer%20in%202%20sentences."   -> 56.4 s, then 46.8 s
$ curl "localhost:8080/recipe?dish=Masala%20Chai"                                           -> 71.6 s (valid Recipe)
  (think=false, same mode: /chat 4.2-5.7 s, /recipe 8.1-12.7 s)

## Why /recipe has the .advisors(AdvisorParams.ENABLE_NATIVE_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT) line (normal mode)
Without the line (Spring AI only asks for JSON in the prompt text):
  Spring AI 2.1.0-M1: 4/5, then 11/20 more  -> 15/25 valid Recipe records (failures: HTTP 500)
  Spring AI 2.1.0 GA: 12/20 valid
  Cause, seen in the request/response to Ollama: in about 4 of 10 answers qwen3.5:4b copied the JSON *schema* back
  ({"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema", "type": "object", ...}) instead of a recipe, so
  "minutes" was missing -> "Cannot map `null` into type `int`" -> HTTP 500.
  Example failed reply (HTTP 500 to the browser):
  {"timestamp":"2026-11-25T09:04:18.172Z","status":500,"error":"Internal Server Error","path":"/recipe"}
With the line (Spring AI sends the Recipe JSON schema to Ollama as its "format", so the model can only answer in that shape):
  normal 5/5 + 20/20 = 25/25 valid; CPU only 5/5 + 20/20 = 25/25 valid.
  Reference: https://docs.spring.io/spring-ai/reference/api/structured-output/native.html

## Spring AI 2.1.0 GA check (final code, normal mode, ./mvnw spring-boot:run -Dspring-ai.version=2.1.0)
$ ./mvnw dependency:tree -Dspring-ai.version=2.1.0  -> spring-ai-ollama:jar:2.1.0, spring-ai-client-chat:jar:2.1.0
/chat  -> answer in 2.0 s (model already loaded)
/recipe -> 5/5 valid, 3.1-3.9 s
/stream -> 4-line poem in 1.1 s
$ ./mvnw test   (the test start.spring.io generates)  -> Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0 -- BUILD SUCCESS

# Note: an M4 Max CPU is fast. An ordinary laptop CPU will be slower (expect several seconds to tens of seconds
# per answer), but it works.
